notes:
Summary (workshop focus):
- Goal: provision Dedicated capacity for customer-facing chat + CS support flows with firm throughput guarantees and P95 latency SLOs.
- Observed baseline: steady-state async load ~45 QPS (user messages that spawn small context), burst traffic pattern up to 220 QPS during marketing spikes.
- Token profile: avg request 180 tokens in, expected 320 tokens generated per response. Baseline tokens/sec steady-state ~14k tok/s; peak bursts up to ~100k tok/s for short windows.
- Latency targets: business asks for P95 <= 150ms for 1-2 turn conversations, CTO quote: "cannot exceed 200ms P95 during peak, otherwise UX team will push back."
- Throughput guarantees: customer wants explicit per-GPU throughput mapping (tokens/sec per H100 / A100) and a failover policy to hosted tier if Dedicated capacity saturated.
- Sizing conclusion (workshop provisional): recommend 6x H100-equivalent GPUs reserved (hot pool) to meet steady-state + 1.5x burst buffer; autoscale policy with warm standby nodes to avoid cold-start latency.
- Cost sensitivity: high; finance asked for committed-month discount and clear burst accounting (separate metering).
- Operational needs: prefix/KV cache important for conversation continuity; prefer workload-aware batching with max-latency budget set to 35ms per batch.
- Routing & fallback: must support regional routing (primary NA, fallback EU-hosted) and deterministic fallback order (Dedicated -> Redwood hosted compatible model -> degraded smaller model).
- Security notes: need SSO (SAML) + audit logs streamed to customer SIEM; KMS integration required for key import.
- POC ask: 2-week parallel run (mirror traffic) with measurement of token/sec and P95 under synthetic and production shadowing.
- Legal: will request SLA credit table aligned to 99.9% uptime and P95 latency tiers; proposed negotiation points: warmup window for new rollouts, maintenance windows 48h notice, data deletion guarantees.
Call quotes/snippets: "We need deterministic billing for bursts — cannot have surprise overages" (Head of Finance).
